prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Katy, Texas, and has whiplash. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1270; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you reported in Katy, Texas. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'm sorry, I'd rather just give you my first name for now. It's part of the accident report anyway.

Q: That's fine. Can you describe in your own words what happened?

A: I was driving on a two-lane road in the early afternoon. A car coming the other way drifted over into my lane. I tried to swerve right, but we still clipped front to front. It wasn't a hard hit, but it was enough to jolt me forward and back.

Q: How fast were you traveling when you first saw the other vehicle?

A: Not very fast, maybe thirty miles an hour or a bit less. The road was wet from a light rain, so I was being careful.

Q: Did either vehicle leave the roadway, or did airbags deploy?

A: No, nothing like that. Both cars stayed on the pavement. My airbag didn't go off.

Q: Were you taken to a medical facility after the collision?

A: My neck and upper back started hurting that evening. The next morning I felt stiff and had headaches. I went to urgent care two days later, and they diagnosed whiplash and gave me a referral for physical therapy.

Q: Have you been able to keep up with your normal activities since then?

A: Some days are harder than others. Lifting my grandchild and sitting at my desk for long periods are the worst. I've missed a few shifts at work because of it.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything you'd like to add before we conclude?

A: Only that I want to make sure my physical therapy bills get covered. I've been keeping every receipt.

Q: Understood. This concludes the recorded statement. Thank you.
